newsitem.title: UK: UK govt ready to forgo BT special share.
newsitem.headline: UK govt ready to forgo BT special share.

text.p: The British government has told British Telecommunications Plc that it is willing to redeem its special share in the company, Trade and Industry Secretary Margaret Beckett said on Tuesday.
The special share effectively gives the government the right to veto any move to allow any shareholder to own more than 15 percent of the voting shares of the company.
The government is also able to use it to block the appointment of an executive chairman who is not a British national.
Industry sources noted there had been press speculation that the existence of the share could hamper the approval by the U.S. authorities of BT's planned merger with MCI Communications Corp.
However they said there had so far been no sign of the share proving a stumbling block to the $24 billion deal.
In a parliamentary written answer announcing the government's willingness to redeem the share, Beckett said: "This decision was taken after careful consideration of the issues involved."

She did not elaborate, but said the move had no implications for special shares which the government has in other companies "where any decision would have to take account of the different circumstances in each case".
Beckett's announcement came on the eve of BT's annual meeting.
